mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over a 3-month window raises discount rates, reducing present value of future corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A strong, sustained rise in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both PAYEMS and UNRATE below their 12-month averages signals a broad-based labor market weakening, which reduces aggregate demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average for four consecutive months signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term consumption demand and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered periods.
